evidence: Plaut. Poen. 43: nunc dum scriblītae aestuant, occurrite
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “a kind of tart”. Cato makes it like his placenta, pastry and cheese in a ring, but without honey; Petronius’s guests eat one cold with hot honey poured over it, in the spelling sciribilīta. Traupman uses the word for a muffin (see “muffin”). For a tart of something else, name the filling, as Traupman does with crustum ex mālīs: scriblīta ex citreīs, a lemon tart. Lewis & Short leaves the first vowel unmarked.

phrases.english: Today we’re going to make a lemon tart.
now, while the tarts are piping hot, run for them!

phrases.latin: Sequēns ferculum fuit sciribilīta frīgida et suprā mel caldum īnfūsum excellente Hispānum.
phrases.english: The next course was a cold tart with hot honey poured over it, the finest Spanish.

sources: Lewis & Short: scriblita · Lewis & Short: crustum
